claim: A vocative is best regarded as a kind of interpolation that can appear in front, central or end position.
evidence_summary: Ch. 15, p. 1350: an interpolation “is located at a position between the beginning and end of a main clause”, and “An appendage is attached loosely at the beginning or end of a clause.” Page 67 draws the same distinction.
finding: Call the vocative a supplement, or say that it is an interpolation in central position and an appendage elsewhere.
proposed_wording: It is best regarded as a kind of supplement, an interpolation in central position and an appendage in front or end position (cf. Ch. 8, §20).
inference: Does the description use interpolation in CGEL’s defined sense?

evidence.establishes: A defined term used outside its definition.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
